title: The Five Scrolls (Megillot)
lead: Five short books in the Writings that Jews read in the synagogue on five occasions of the year: Song of Songs, Ruth, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes and Esther.

sections.b: Custom assigns the Song of Songs to Passover, Ruth to the Festival of Weeks (Shavuot), Lamentations to the Ninth of Av, Ecclesiastes to the Festival of Booths (Sukkot) and Esther to Purim. The reading of Esther at Purim is ancient (Mishnah Megillah); the habit of reading the other four on their days developed later. In the Hebrew Bible the five stand in the Writings, the third part of the canon, and the Christian Old Testament scatters them (Ruth after Judges; Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes with the wisdom books; Lamentations after Jeremiah; Esther among the histories).
sections.refs: Song of Songs 1:1; Ruth 1:1; Lamentations 1:1; Ecclesiastes 1:1; Esther 1:1

sections.b: Some of the matches are clear (Esther and Purim; Lamentations and the fall of the temple), and some are loose: Ruth is a harvest story and Weeks is a harvest festival; Ecclesiastes' "vanity" suits Booths when the harvest is in and the year is turning. No ancient text explains why the five were grouped.
